sundar.39.cau1: Dear brother, Śrī Rāma is not a king among men: he is lord of all the worlds, the Death even of Death. He is Brahman, the Lord, free from all ills and unborn, all-pervading, unconquerable, without beginning and without end.
sundar.39.cau2: The ocean of mercy, who works for the good of the earth, the brāhmaṇas, the cows and the gods, has taken a human body. He delights his devotees, destroys the hosts of the wicked and guards the Vedas and dharma. Listen, brother.
sundar.39.cau3: Give up your enmity and bow your head to him; Śrī Rāma ends the suffering of all who bow to him. My lord, give Vaidehī back to the Lord, and worship Śrī Rāma, who loves without any motive.
sundar.39.cau4: The Lord does not cast off even one who carries the sin of having wronged the whole world, once he goes to him for refuge. The very Lord whose name ends the three afflictions has appeared; understand this in your heart, Rāvaṇa.
sundar.39.do39क: Rāvaṇa, I fall at your feet over and over and entreat you: cast off pride, delusion and arrogance, and worship the Lord of Kosala.
sundar.39.do39ख: The sage Pulastya sent this message by way of his own disciple. Dear brother, finding a good moment, I have told it straight away to you, my lord.
sundar.40.cau1: Mālyavān was a minister of great wisdom. He was much pleased to hear these words, and said: Dear one, your younger brother is an ornament of good counsel; take to heart what Vibhīṣaṇa is saying.
sundar.40.cau2: Rāvaṇa said: These two fools are praising the enemy. Will no one take them away? Is anyone there? Mālyavān then went home, and Vibhīṣaṇa, joining his palms, spoke again:
sundar.40.cau3: Good sense and ill sense dwell in every heart, my lord; so say the Purāṇas and the Vedas. Where there is good sense, there is prosperity of every kind; where there is ill sense, calamity comes in the end.
sundar.40.cau4: A perverse ill sense has settled in your heart, so you take a well-wisher for a foe and an enemy for a friend. You have a great love for Sītā, who is the night of doom for the race of demons.
sundar.40.do40: Dear brother, I clasp your feet and ask you: grant this for love of me. Give Sītā to Śrī Rāma, so that no harm comes to you.
sundar.41.cau1: Vibhīṣaṇa spoke words of right counsel, in agreement with the wise, the Purāṇas and the Vedas. On hearing them, Rāvaṇa rose in fury and said: Wretch, your death is now close at hand.
sundar.41.cau2: Fool, you have always lived because I let you live, and yet, simpleton, you favour the enemy's side. Tell me, wretch: who is there in the world whom I have not conquered by the strength of my arms?
sundar.41.cau3: You live in my city and love those ascetics. Fool, go and join them, and preach your counsel to them. With these words he kicked him, and his younger brother clasped his feet again and again.
sundar.41.cau4: Umā, this is the greatness of a saint: he does good even to one who does him harm. Vibhīṣaṇa said: You stand in a father's place for me; you were right to strike me. But it is in worshipping Śrī Rāma that your good lies, my lord.
sundar.41.cau5: With his ministers, Vibhīṣaṇa rose into the sky and went off, saying this for all to hear:
sundar.41.do41: Śrī Rāma is the Lord whose resolve always comes true, and your court is in the grip of death. I go now to take refuge with Śrī Rāma; do not lay the blame on me.
sundar.42.cau1: As soon as Vibhīṣaṇa set off, saying this, all of them were doomed to die. Pārvatī, scorn shown to a holy man at once destroys every good.
sundar.42.cau2: The moment Rāvaṇa cast Vibhīṣaṇa off, the luckless king lost all his splendour. Vibhīṣaṇa set out joyfully for Śrī Rāma, cherishing many hopes in his heart.
sundar.42.cau3: I shall go and see those lotus feet, rosy and soft, that bring joy to his servants: the feet whose touch saved the sage's wife, Ahalyā, and which made the Daṇḍaka forest holy.
sundar.42.cau4: The feet that Sītā, Janaka's daughter, holds to her heart, that ran over the ground after the deceitful deer, that bloom as lotuses in the lake that is Śiva's heart: what good fortune! I shall see those very feet.
sundar.42.do42: The feet on whose sandals Bharata has set his mind: today I shall go and behold those feet with these eyes of mine.
sundar.43.cau1: Thinking such loving thoughts, Vibhīṣaṇa soon reached this shore of the ocean. The monkeys saw him approaching and thought he must be an important envoy of the enemy.
sundar.43.cau2: Keeping him there, they went to the king of the monkeys and reported everything to him. Sugrīva said: O Lord of the Raghus, hear this: Rāvaṇa's brother is here to meet you.
sundar.43.cau3: The Lord said: Friend, what do you make of it? The king of the monkeys said: Listen, O king of men: no one can see through the wiles of the demons. Who knows why this shape-changer has come?
sundar.43.cau4: The wretch has come to learn our secrets; I think we should keep him in bonds. The Lord said: Friend, you have weighed the policy well, but I am pledged to remove the fear of whoever comes to me for refuge.
sundar.43.cau5: Hanumān rejoiced at the Lord's words: the Lord is loving to those who seek his refuge.
sundar.43.do43: Those who abandon one who has come to them for refuge, judging that he may do them harm, are base and full of sin; there is harm in even looking at them.
sundar.44.cau1: Even one who bears the guilt of killing millions of brāhmaṇas I do not abandon once he comes to me for refuge. The moment a soul turns to face me, the sins of millions of births are destroyed.
sundar.44.cau2: It is the very nature of a sinner that worship of me never pleases him. If he were truly wicked at heart, would he come before me?
sundar.44.cau3: Only one whose mind is pure finds me; deceit, cunning and fault-finding do not please me. Should Rāvaṇa have sent him here to learn our secrets, still, king of the monkeys, we have nothing to fear and nothing to lose.
sundar.44.cau4: Friend, Lakṣmaṇa can kill in the blink of an eye every demon there is in the world. And if he has come to me for refuge out of fear, I will guard him as I guard my own life.
sundar.44.do44: The abode of mercy said with a smile: Bring him in either case. Crying victory to the compassionate Lord, the monkeys set off, with Aṅgada and Hanumān.
sundar.45.cau1: Respectfully placing him in front, the monkeys went to where Śrī Rāma, the mine of compassion, was. From far off Vibhīṣaṇa saw the two brothers, who give the gift of joy to the eyes.
sundar.45.cau2: Then, as he looked upon Śrī Rāma, abode of all beauty, he stood rooted, gazing unblinking, his eyelids held still. The Lord's arms were long, his eyes like red lotuses, his body dark, freeing from fear those who bow to him.
sundar.45.cau3: His shoulders were like a lion's and his broad chest shone; his face would charm the hearts of countless gods of love. Vibhīṣaṇa's eyes filled with tears and his whole body thrilled; steadying his mind, he spoke gently:
sundar.45.cau4: I am the brother of Rāvaṇa, my Lord, and was born in the race of demons, O protector of the gods. My body is of the dark quality (tamas) and by nature fond of sin, as the owl loves the darkness.
sundar.45.do45: I have come, Lord, having heard with my ears your fair fame, that you destroy the distress of worldly existence. Save me, save me, remover of suffering, giver of joy to those who seek refuge, O hero of the Raghus.
sundar.46.cau1: Seeing him prostrate himself after these words, the Lord rose at once, full of joy. The humble words pleased the Lord's heart; he gathered him in his mighty arms and held him to his heart.
sundar.46.cau2: Meeting him together with his younger brother, he seated him close by, and the Lord, who takes away his devotees' fear, said: Tell me, Lord of Laṅkā, how you and your family are; you live in an evil place.
sundar.46.cau3: You dwell day and night among a company of the wicked; how do you keep to dharma, friend? Your ways are all known to me: you are deeply versed in right conduct, and wrong does not please you.
sundar.46.cau4: Even a dwelling in hell is better, dear one; may the Creator never grant the company of the wicked. Vibhīṣaṇa said: O Lord of the Raghus, now that I have seen your feet I am well, for you have shown me mercy, knowing me as your servant.
sundar.46.do46: A soul knows no well-being, and its mind no rest even in a dream, until it gives up desire, the home of sorrow, and worships Śrī Rāma.
sundar.47.cau1: Many wicked ones, greed, delusion, envy, pride and vanity, dwell in the heart for as long as Śrī Rāma, holding his bow and arrows, with a quiver at his waist, does not dwell there.
sundar.47.cau2: Attachment is a pitch-dark night at its height, which delights the owls of craving and aversion. It lives in a soul's mind only until the Lord's majesty rises there like the sun.
sundar.47.cau3: Now I am well and my great fears are gone, O Rāma, for my eyes have seen your lotus feet. O compassionate Lord, the one to whom you are gracious is never touched by the three kinds of worldly pain.
sundar.47.cau4: I am a demon of very base nature and have never done a good deed. Yet the Lord, whose form does not come even into the meditation of sages, has joyfully clasped me to his heart.
sundar.47.do47: What good fortune is mine, boundless beyond measure, O Rāma, mass of grace and joy: with my own eyes I have seen the pair of lotus feet that Brahmā and Śiva serve.
